title: Some Reformed answer more loosely: foreknowledge brings a necessity, but not of coaction or physical determination
source_text: XXVIII. Simplicius autem adhuc & confusius ad hanc difficultatem respondent ex Doctoribus Reformatis nonnulli, Dei praescientiam rebus omnibus futuris necessitatem quidem aliquam inducere, sed non omnem necessitatem cum libertate pugnare; verum illam duntaxat quae est a coactione, aut a determinatione Physica.
pass_a_gloss: XXVIII. But some of the Reformed Doctors respond to this difficulty more simply still and more confusedly, that the foreknowledge of God induces indeed some necessity on all future things, but that not every necessity conflicts with liberty; but that only which is from coaction, or from Physical determination.
pass_b_english: Some Reformed teachers answer the difficulty in a still simpler and less precise way. They say that God's foreknowledge does bring a certain necessity upon all future things, but that not every necessity is at odds with freedom. Only necessity arising from compulsion or from physical determination conflicts with it.

lemmas.gloss: more simply still and more confusedly

lemmas.latin: a coactione, aut a determinatione Physica
lemmas.gloss: from coaction, or from Physical determination

choices.why: The Schools distinguish the necessity of the consequence (hypothetical) from the necessity of the consequent (absolute); the technical pair is kept so the argument stays exact.
